caption: A page of the Codex Cruz-Badianus (Libellus de Medicinalibus Indorum Herbis, 1552) showing three plants under their Nahuatl names: mecaxochitl, tlilxochitl huey nacaztli, and copalxococtl.
alt: Sixteenth-century manuscript page with hand-painted illustrations of three flowering plants with root bulbs, each labeled with a Nahuatl name in red ink, above a block of Latin text.
credit: Wikimedia Commons, Libellus de Medicinalibus Indorum Herbis (Codex Cruz-Badianus), folio 56v
note: Contextual image, not from the document: no digitisation of El México Antiguo vol. 1 (1919) or a portrait of Reko could be found, so this uses a folio of the 1552 Nahua herbal that itself labels plants with the Nahuatl names Reko's article discusses. Distinct from the 1615 Ximénez Hernández edition and the Florentine Codex image used elsewhere in this archive.
